correctness.rationale: An exact Q(sqrt5) checker verifies the specified ten vertices, all twenty edges, the five non-coplanar antipodal vertex-normal directions, and 22 distinct integer strict witnesses. The great-circle chamber-count theorem proves these witnesses exhaustive, establishing that only six and ten edges can be cut by any generic central plane. The exact equal-edge central cosine and elementary Haar crossing identity determine the two probabilities. The finite certificate is exhaustive, not a simulation.

value.rationale: A classical regular antiprism has a natural uniform central-plane section statistic. Its complete law consists of only two polygon types and a structurally forbidden octagon even though the polyhedron has enough vertices and edges for that intermediate count. Exact probabilities follow from a motivated geometric cut classification; this is a complete nontrivial invariant with reproducible sharp evidence.
